title: Cosmic Latte: The Average Color of the Universe
explanation:
# The Universe's True Color

When astronomers averaged the light from 200,000 galaxies, they discovered that if you could smear the entire cosmos across the sky, it would glow a warm beige—a shade so perfectly mundane it earned the winning nickname "cosmic latte." This surprising color reveals something profound: the universe is becoming redder over time as older, cooler stars gradually outnumber hot blue ones, painting a portrait of cosmic aging written in light itself.
